title: Pre-Gym Nutrition Guide
meta_desc: Discover the best foods to eat before the gym in NZ, including meal timing, quick options and affordable protein sources to boost your fitness programme
intro: As a gym-goer in New Zealand, it's essential to fuel your body with the right foods before a workout to optimise performance and support your fitness goals. Eating the right foods at the right time can make all the difference in your energy levels and overall exercise experience. In this guide, we'll explore the best foods to eat before the gym, including meal timing, quick options from NZ supermarkets, and affordable protein sources.

sections.heading: Meal Timing: When to Eat Before the Gym
sections.body: Aim to eat a meal or snack 1-3 hours before your gym session. This allows for adequate digestion and energy release. If you're someone who prefers to train on an empty stomach, also known as fasted training, be aware of the potential pros and cons. Fasted training can improve mental toughness and boost fat burning, but it may also lead to decreased performance and muscle loss if not done correctly.
list: 1-3 hours before: eat a balanced meal with complex carbohydrates and protein
30 minutes to 1 hour before: opt for a light snack or energy drink
On an empty stomach: consider fasted training, but be mindful of potential drawbacks

sections.heading: Quick and Affordable Options from NZ Supermarkets
sections.body: NZ supermarkets like Countdown, New World, and Pak'nSave offer a range of quick and affordable food options that are perfect for pre-gym meals. Some examples include whole grain bread with peanut butter and banana, Greek yoghurt with berries and honey, or a handful of nuts and dried fruit. You can also find affordable protein sources like chicken breast, tuna, and eggs.
list: Whole grain bread with peanut butter and banana ($2-$3)
Greek yoghurt with berries and honey ($3-$4)

sections.heading: Simple Carb and Protein Combos for Energy
sections.body: Combining carbohydrates and protein is essential for providing energy and supporting muscle function during exercise. Some simple and effective combos include whole grain toast with avocado and eggs, oatmeal with banana and almond butter, or a protein smoothie with Greek yoghurt and berries. You can also consider adding affordable NZ protein supplements like whey protein or plant-based alternatives to your diet.
list: Whole grain toast with avocado and eggs
Oatmeal with banana and almond butter
Protein smoothie with Greek yoghurt and berries

sections.heading: Conclusion and Next Steps
sections.body: By following these simple and evidence-based guidelines, you can optimise your pre-gym nutrition and support your fitness goals. Remember to stay hydrated, listen to your body, and adjust your meal timing and food choices based on your individual needs.
